back_translation: The word of the LORD that came to Jeremiah concerning the drought.
Judah mourns, and her gates languish; the people are in dark gloom down to the ground, and the cry of Jerusalem goes up.
The nobles send their servants for water; they go to the cisterns but find no water; their vessels return empty. They are ashamed and humiliated, so they cover their heads.
Because the ground is cracked since no rain has fallen on the land, the farmers are ashamed; they cover their heads.
Even the doe in the field gives birth and forsakes it, because there is no grass.
Wild donkeys stand on the bare heights; they pant for air like jackals; their eyes grow dim because there is no vegetation.
O LORD, though our iniquities testify against us, act for the sake of your name; for our backslidings are many; we have sinned against you.
O Hope of Israel, its Savior in time of distress, why are you like a stranger in the land, like a traveler who turns aside to lodge but one night?
Why are you like a man dumbfounded, like a warrior who cannot save? Yet you are in our midst, O LORD, and we are called by your name; do not forsake us.

Thus says the LORD concerning this people: They truly love to wander; they have not restrained their feet. Therefore the LORD does not accept them; now he will remember their iniquity and punish their sins.
The LORD said to me, 'Do not pray for the welfare of this people.'
Although they fast, I will not listen to their cry; although they offer burnt offerings and grain offerings, I will not accept them; but I will consume them by sword, famine, and plague.
Then I said, 'Ah, Lord GOD! Behold, the prophets are telling them, "You will not see the sword, and famine will not come to you, but I will give you true peace in this place."'

The LORD said to me, 'The prophets are prophesying lies in my name; I did not send them, nor command them, nor speak to them. They are prophesying to you a false vision, worthless divination, a worthless thing, and the deceit of their own minds.'

Therefore thus says the LORD concerning the prophets who prophesy in my name though I did not send them, and who say, 'Sword and famine will not come to this land': by sword and famine those prophets themselves will meet their end.

And the people to whom they prophesy will be thrown out into the streets of Jerusalem because of famine and sword, and no one will bury them—them, their wives, their sons, and their daughters; and I will pour out their own evil upon them.
You shall say to them this word: 'Let my eyes run with tears night and day, and not cease, for the virgin daughter of my people has been shattered with a great wound, a very grievous blow.'
If I go out to the field, behold, those slain by the sword; if I enter the city, behold, those sick from famine; for both prophet and priest are taken to a land they do not know.

Have you utterly rejected Judah? Does your soul loathe Zion? Why have you struck us so that there is no healing for us? We hoped for peace, but no good came; for a time of healing, but behold, terror.
O LORD, we acknowledge our wickedness and the iniquity of our fathers, for we have sinned against you.
For the sake of your name do not despise us; do not dishonor your glorious throne. Remember, do not break your covenant with us.

Among the worthless idols of the nations, is there any that can bring rain? Or can the heavens give showers of themselves? Are you not he, O LORD our God? So we hope in you, for you have made all these things.
